summary: End-to-end REST API testing of the Brand Library feature. 17/17 new API tests in test_brand_library_api.py passed, and the 15/15 pre-existing unit tests in test_brand_library.py still pass. Covered brand-kit GET/PUT round-trip, asset upload/list/filter/patch/delete, public file streaming, model normalization (invalid type/category fallback), RBAC for super_admin vs regular user vs other-company user, cross-tenant isolation, and the /api/agent/sessions/{id}/media-config persistence of useBrandLibrary + brandLibraryMode.

minor.issue: Backend sets `Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600` but the Cloudflare/K8s ingress in the preview environment rewrites it to `no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate`. The asset still streams with correct Content-Type and bytes. Worth confirming whether you want caching in production (this may also rewrite there) — if yes the ingress / Cloudflare cache rule needs to be relaxed for /api/companies/*/assets/*/file.

action_items: Optional: investigate whether the Cache-Control override by the edge proxy is intentional. If brand assets should be cacheable in browsers/CDNs, the proxy rule for /api/companies/*/assets/*/file needs adjustment.

Consider documenting that company_assets_meta and company_assets are now produced by tests. The new API test_brand_library_api.py prefixes all test rows with TEST_ and cleans them up at the end of TestAssetCRUD.
critical_code_review_comments: company_assets.py uses `user.get("role")` for the own-company RBAC check (line 61/98). This only honors the legacy single-`role` field. Users whose super_admin status is stored only in the newer `roles: [..]` array would NOT bypass the company check here (the require_super_admin dependency uses has_role which handles both fields, so this is still safe for super_admin mutations — but a super_admin reading another company's brand-kit via GET when their record only has roles=['super_admin'] and role unset would get a 403 even though they should see everything). Recommend reusing has_role(user, 'super_admin') in get_brand_kit and list_assets.

upload_asset reads the entire file into memory (await file.read()) AND writes it to a NamedTemporaryFile AND base64-encodes it inside store_company_asset_async — three copies of the bytes simultaneously. Fine for the current ~MB image budget but worth bounding with a max upload size check at the route boundary to avoid OOM on a malicious large upload.

delete_asset is a hard delete and does not check whether the asset is referenced by any active project/slide. If a course was generated using an asset URL and the super_admin deletes the asset, exported SCORM packages that have already embedded the bytes are fine, but a re-export or live preview would 404. Consider soft delete (set isActive=false) as default and a confirm flag for hard delete, OR scan slides for references before deleting.
Cache-Control header set in serve_asset is being stripped by the edge ingress (see minor issue above) — header rule may need a complementary `s-maxage` or a different header the proxy preserves.
